blocks.text: Most people start by scrolling the sidebar. They look for #marketing or a teammate's name, then click. That works, but it slows down once the sidebar gets long and the name you need sits far down the list. The keyboard route is faster, and it works the same way every time.

Slack's help article on keyboard navigation calls this action Open a conversation. It covers channels and direct messages alike. You press one shortcut, type a few letters, and choose the match. The rest of this page walks through that flow, then covers the cases where it goes wrong.
Jump to a conversation on Mac with ⌘ K

The steps below cover the Slack desktop app for Mac. Slack also runs in a browser, and browsers sometimes claim shortcuts before Slack sees them. Windows and Linux use Ctrl K instead of ⌘ K, so if a colleague sends you a Windows tip, swap the key and the rest stays the same.
That's the whole process. After a few days, your hand goes to ⌘ K before your eyes reach the sidebar. The sidebar still matters for browsing, but you stop using it to find names you already know.
Open a conversation in a new window

Sometimes you want two conversations on screen at once. Slack can open a channel or direct message in its own window. Move focus onto the conversation's name in the sidebar, then press ⌘ Enter. Your main window stays on the conversation it was showing.

Here's a worked example. You're reading #launch-checklist when a billing question lands in #support. Press ⌘ K, type support, and press Enter to move there. If you'd rather keep the launch channel open, focus #support in the sidebar and press ⌘ Enter. You get a second window with the support conversation in it.
Jump to a direct message the same way

Direct messages follow the same pattern. Press ⌘ K, type the person's name, and wait for the match to appear. A few letters are usually enough, but common first names can return several people. Check the full name or the team before you press Enter.
Quick switching versus searching messages

⌘ K and ⌘ G do different jobs, and mixing them up wastes time. ⌘ K takes you to a place, a channel or a person. ⌘ G starts a search, which is what you need when you know the words someone wrote but not where they wrote them.
Use ⌘ K when you know the name. Use search when you know the words. If you need a phrase inside one conversation, the search guide linked at the end of this page covers that case.
Mistakes that cost people time

items: Using Ctrl K on a Mac. Ctrl K is the Windows and Linux shortcut. On a Mac, use ⌘ K.
Hunting through menus for a Jump to command. Slack's help pages don't give a Mac menu path for this action, so the keyboard is the reliable route.
Pressing Enter before reading the highlighted match. Two people can share a first name, and the wrong conversation opens without a second check.
Expecting ⌘ K to work while another app is in front. Click the Slack window, or press ⌘ Tab to bring Slack forward, then try again.
Using Cmd F in a browser and landing in the browser's find bar. The troubleshooting section below covers the setting that changes this.

blocks.text: Most of these mistakes take a few seconds to fix. The first one causes the most confusion, because it looks like a broken shortcut when you are simply pressing the wrong key.
Shortcuts to learn next to ⌘ K
⌘ K is the one to learn first. The table lists the shortcuts that sit beside it in Slack's keyboard help pages. Keep the table in a note while you practice, then close it once the keys feel familiar.

blocks.text: The ⌘ / list is the most reliable reference because it shows the shortcuts your build supports. Copied lists on blogs and forums can be older than the app on your Mac, so trust the list inside Slack when the two disagree.
A one-week practice plan for ⌘ K

items: Day 1: use ⌘ K for every channel switch, even when you could click.
Day 2: use ⌘ K to open direct messages, and check the full name before Enter.
Day 3: open one conversation in a new window with ⌘ Enter, then close it when you're done.
Day 4: use ⌘ G to search for words, and keep ⌘ K for names.
Day 5: open ⌘ / once, and pick one shortcut you didn't know to add.

blocks.text: Keep the plan short. One new step a day beats trying every shortcut at once. By the end of the week, the switch to a conversation should take less thought than the click it replaced.
Check your Slack version before November 9, 2026

Shortcuts and menus change between releases, so know which build you run. The latest Mac release confirmed for this guide is 4.53.280, a security update dated November 3, 2026. Slack's Mac release notes page lists each build with its date, so check it when a shortcut stops behaving.

The deadline is close. Slack ends support for macOS 13 and below on November 9, 2026. It also ends support for Slack Mac app 4.46.104 and below on the same date. If either applies to you, update now rather than waiting for the last day.
What the Free plan means for search and history

Slack's pricing page says messages on the Free plan are saved and searchable for 90 days. It also says Free Slack deletes data after one year. Pro lists unlimited message history. The shortcut opens a conversation, so it doesn't search old messages. The 90-day limit applies when you search.
If your team runs on Free, put decisions in a channel where people will look for them. Older messages may fall out of search reach before anyone thinks to go back for them.
When ⌘ K does nothing: causes and fixes
Most failures come from three causes. Slack isn't the active app, your keyboard layout is wrong, or your build is too old. Check the active app first, because it's the quickest to rule out.
Keyboard layout is the cause people change by mistake. Slack lets you set the layout only when it can't detect your keyboard. If your keys work everywhere else on the Mac, leave that setting alone.
Use Cmd F for Slack search in a browser

If you use Slack in a browser, Cmd F can open the browser's find bar instead of Slack search. Slack's search preferences article describes a setting that changes this. Open your profile picture, choose Preferences, then Advanced, and turn on the option under Search options that lets Cmd F start a Slack search.
Desktop app or browser: which one to use

This guide assumes the desktop app. Slack's keyboard shortcuts page marks ⌘ J as working only in the desktop app, so the desktop app is the safer choice for these shortcuts. Slack's help pages don't document every difference between the desktop app and the browser version. When a shortcut acts differently, open ⌘ / and trust the list for your build.
Where to go next

If the conversation you need has unread messages, [jump to the latest unread message in Slack on Mac](/how-to/jump-to-the-latest-unread-message-in-slack) with ⌘ J. To find a specific message inside a conversation, read [how to search inside a conversation in Slack on Mac](/how-to/search-inside-a-conversation-in-slack). For every shortcut in the app, see [how to show keyboard shortcuts in Slack on Mac](/how-to/show-the-keyboard-shortcuts-list-in-slack).
Start with ⌘ K for one workday. Once it feels normal, add the unread and search shortcuts one at a time, not all at once.

faq.question: What is the shortcut to jump to a conversation in Slack on Mac?
faq.answer: Press ⌘ K, type the name of the channel or person, then press Enter. Slack's Navigate with your keyboard article describes the same steps. Windows and Linux use Ctrl K for the same job.

faq.question: Is there a menu item for jumping to a conversation on Mac?
faq.answer: Slack's help pages don't give a Mac menu path for this action, so the keyboard is the reliable route. If you find a menu item in your version, use it, but the ⌘ K shortcut works the same way.

faq.question: How do I open a conversation in a new window in Slack on Mac?
faq.answer: Move focus onto the conversation's name in the sidebar, then press ⌘ Enter. The channel or direct message opens in its own window, and your main window keeps its place.

faq.question: Why does ⌘ K do nothing on my Mac?
faq.answer: Check that Slack is the active app first. Then check your keyboard layout and your Slack version. Slack lets you change the layout only when it can't detect your keyboard.

faq.question: Does ⌘ J jump to unread messages in Slack?
faq.answer: Yes. Slack's keyboard shortcuts page lists ⌘ J for jumping to the most recent unread message in a conversation. That shortcut works only in the Slack desktop app.

faq.question: Which Slack version is current for Mac?
faq.answer: The latest Mac release confirmed for this guide is 4.53.280, dated November 3, 2026, a security update. Check Slack's release notes page for anything newer before you rely on a specific build.

faq.question: Do I need to update before November 9, 2026?
faq.answer: Yes, if you run macOS 13 or older, or Slack 4.46.104 or older. Slack ends support for both on November 9, 2026, so update before that date.

steps.name: Make Slack the active app
steps.text: Click inside the Slack window, or press ⌘ Tab until Slack is highlighted. Keyboard shortcuts go to the app in front, so Slack has to be in front first.
steps.tip: Click the Slack window once if the keys seem to do nothing.

steps.name: Press ⌘ K
steps.text: Hold Command, tap K, and let go. A search box opens over the window, ready for typing. You don't need to click it first.
steps.tip: On Windows and Linux the same step uses Ctrl K.

steps.name: Type the channel or person's name
steps.text: Type a few letters of the name. Channel names appear with a hash mark, such as #design. Matches update as you type. Stop once you see the one you want.
steps.tip: Type the full name if the list shows several close matches.

steps.name: Check the match before you press Enter
steps.text: Read the full name next to each match. Two people can share a first name, and the wrong one is easy to open. Look at the team or channel name when two matches look alike.

steps.name: Press Enter
steps.text: Press Enter, which Mac keyboards label Return. Slack opens the conversation you picked, and the window moves to that channel or person.
steps.tip: Enter opens the match that is selected, so check it first.

steps.name: Confirm you're in the right place
steps.text: Look at the conversation's name at the top of the window before you read or reply. If it's the wrong one, press ⌘ K again and type a more specific name.

troubleshooting.problem: ⌘ K does nothing or types into another app
troubleshooting.fix: Click the Slack window first, or press ⌘ Tab to bring Slack forward. Then try ⌘ K again. Keyboard shortcuts only reach the app in front.

troubleshooting.problem: Letters look wrong when you type the name
troubleshooting.fix: Your keyboard layout may be set wrong. Open your profile picture, choose Preferences, then Language & region, and check Keyboard layout. Change it only if Slack can't detect your keyboard.

troubleshooting.problem: ⌘ F opens the browser's find bar instead of Slack search
troubleshooting.fix: Turn on the Cmd F option under Preferences > Advanced > Search options. Slack's search preferences article is written for browser use.
Update Slack. Slack ends support for Slack Mac app 4.46.104 and below on November 9, 2026, so update before that date.

troubleshooting.problem: Your Mac runs macOS 13 or older
troubleshooting.fix: Slack ends support for macOS 13 and below on November 9, 2026. Update macOS if your Mac supports a newer version, or plan a replacement before that date.

troubleshooting.problem: The person or channel never appears in the list
troubleshooting.fix: Check the spelling, then check that you're in the right workspace. If you use more than one workspace, the name may belong to another one.
